Synopsis:
The ECB is virtually certain to hike rates 25bps to 2.5% in September, driven by energy-pushed inflation back above 3%. Further hikes beyond September are possible but unlikely, with markets pricing some chance by December. New ECB projections are expected broadly unchanged, though 2026 growth may be nudged higher. Key uncertainties center on second-round inflation effects from energy, a softening labor market, and rising global bond yields. The article also flags friction over a unilateral U.S. FX intervention selling euros to support the yen, which annoyed European officials but has limited direct policy implications.
